subject.title: security fix(gateway): defend pre-auth device-signature verify against CPU DoS

question: Should OpenClaw accept this layered pre-auth device-signature mitigation, including the new device field caps and canonical rate_limited lockout contract, as the gateway security-boundary fix for the linked CPU DoS?
rationale: The code path is security-sensitive and changes protocol validation plus unauthenticated auth throttling semantics, which automation should not approve without owner intent even when the patch looks correct.

options.title: Approve after refreshed proof
options.body: Require a current-head terminal or live gateway transcript showing the AUTH_RATE_LIMITED lockout contract, then proceed with security-owner approval.

options.title: Accept existing proof
options.body: Treat the older proof plus green focused tests as sufficient because the latest commit only changes the response contract, accepting the remaining proof gap.

options.title: Request narrower split
options.body: Ask the contributor to split protocol bounds, shape checks, and the limiter gate if owners want each security-layer decision reviewed separately.
